_meta.tool: Pet Behavior Decoder (id: PetWeirdnessDecoder — display name only, see notes)
_meta.how_to_regression_diff: Re-run cases (npm run check:golden pet-weirdness-decoder). Diff for QUALITY not exact match: HTTP 200, no truncation. V2 REWRITE (2026-09-05): replaces likelihood-scored differentials, breed genetic-predisposition lists, arbitrary age-bucket rules, invented prevalence ('how common'), fabricated community anecdotes, and behavior-modification timelines ('improvement in 1-3 weeks') with plausible explanations grounded only in what was reported, what would make each more or less likely, and observable next-step triggers instead of a countdown. Old schema (behavior_analysis/breed_specific_info/life_stage_context/most_likely_explanation/how_common/other_possibilities with likelihood/when_to_worry/vet_visit_prep/if_its_just_quirky/behavioral_modification/similar_pet_stories) fully replaced by: assessment{action_level,headline,bottom_line} / what_you_reported[] / what_could_explain_it[]{possibility,why_it_could_fit,what_would_make_it_more_or_less_plausible[]} / what_to_watch[] / what_would_change_the_next_step[] / what_you_can_do_now[] / vet_prep{show_only_when_useful,what_to_record[],questions_or_details_to_bring[]}. action_level is one of likely_low_concern|watch_closely|vet_contact_recommended|emergency — never a percentage, never high/medium/low. Added router.outputStandard='v2' + router.outputGuard with runOutputGuard (LLM-judge check + repair), since the failure modes here are invented FACTS (a symptom, a trigger, a medication effect) that a regex can't reliably catch — matches the Party Architect precedent, not PEP's regex-only approach. Fixed a pre-existing anti-pattern in the /followup endpoint: raw anthropic.messages.create with a hand-rolled 3-try loop, now callClaudeWithRetry with a {"answer": "..."} JSON envelope (callClaudeWithRetry always JSON.parses — there is no free-text mode). Also fixed: an 'AI-assisted' mention in the vet summary footer, present in all 13 languages since the tool shipped, and a display-name rename (Pet Weirdness Decoder → Pet Behavior Decoder) that deliberately keeps id/route/i18n prefix unchanged (see tool-notes) — this golden file's tool name in the header reflects the NEW display name, but the endpoint path is unchanged. DO NOT reintroduce: likelihood labels on possibilities, breed/age as anything but situational context, invented prevalence, community anecdotes, or a behavior-mod timeline.

input.behavior: For the past week she's been yowling at 3am, running laps around the apartment, and knocking things off shelves. She's spayed and indoor-only. Nothing in the environment has changed.
input.whenItHappens: Mostly around 3am, then she settles down after 15-20 minutes.

assessment.headline: Nächtliches Schreien und Aktivitätsschübe um 3 Uhr
assessment.bottom_line: Das Muster – kurze, wiederkehrende Aktivitätsschübe nachts ohne weitere Veränderungen – könnte mehrere Erklärungen haben. Da keine anderen Anzeichen gemeldet wurden, lohnt sich eine Beobachtung der nächsten ein bis zwei Wochen, um zu sehen, ob sich das Verhalten verändert oder sich ein klarer Auslöser abzeichnet.

what_you_reported: Weibliche Katze, 4 Jahre alt, kastriert, Wohnungskatze
Seit einer Woche: lautes Schreien, Rennen und Gegenstände herunterschmeißen – hauptsächlich gegen 3 Uhr nachts
Die Episoden dauern jeweils etwa 15–20 Minuten, danach beruhigt sie sich wieder
Keine gemeldeten Veränderungen in Umgebung, Futter, Gesundheit oder Medikamenten
Keine früheren gespeicherten Beobachtungen zu diesem Verhalten

what_could_explain_it.possibility: Nächtliche Aktivitätsphasen als Teil des natürlichen Aktivitätsrhythmus
what_could_explain_it.why_it_could_fit: Katzen sind von Natur aus in der Dämmerung und nachts aktiv; auch kastrierte Wohnungskatzen können ausgeprägte Aktivitätsschübe zu bestimmten Nachtzeiten entwickeln.
what_would_make_it_more_or_less_plausibl: Eher wahrscheinlich, wenn die Katze tagsüber viel schläft und abends wenig Beschäftigung hat
Weniger wahrscheinlich, wenn das Schreien anhaltend und intensiv klingt und nicht durch Rennen oder Spielen unterbrochen wird
Weniger wahrscheinlich, wenn das Schreien auch zu anderen Tageszeiten neu aufgetreten ist

what_could_explain_it.possibility: Reaktion auf etwas außerhalb der Wohnung, das du nicht wahrnimmst
what_could_explain_it.why_it_could_fit: Geräusche, Gerüche oder Bewegungen von anderen Tieren, Nachbarn oder draußen könnten zu dieser Uhrzeit für die Katze wahrnehmbar sein, ohne dass du etwas bemerkst.
what_would_make_it_more_or_less_plausibl: Eher wahrscheinlich, wenn die Episoden immer in der Nähe von Fenstern oder Türen stattfinden
Eher wahrscheinlich, wenn sich die Katze bei den Episoden auf etwas außerhalb zu konzentrieren scheint
Weniger wahrscheinlich, wenn sie sich gleichmäßig durch alle Räume bewegt ohne erkennbaren Fokus

what_could_explain_it.possibility: Körperliches Unwohlsein oder eine beginnende gesundheitliche Veränderung
what_could_explain_it.why_it_could_fit: Vermehrtes Schreien kann gelegentlich mit körperlichem Unbehagen zusammenhängen, lässt sich aber nicht ohne weitere Anzeichen von anderen Erklärungen unterscheiden.
what_would_make_it_more_or_less_plausibl: Eher bedenkenswert, wenn zusätzlich Veränderungen beim Fressen, Trinken, Katzenklo-Nutzung oder im Allgemeinzustand auftreten
Eher bedenkenswert, wenn das Schreien sich verändert – zum Beispiel klagender oder anhaltender wird
Weniger wahrscheinlich, wenn die Katze tagsüber völlig unauffällig ist und die Episoden klar mit Bewegung und Spielverhalten verknüpft sind

what_to_watch: Veränderungen beim Fressen, Trinken oder der Nutzung der Katzentoilette
Ob das Schreien sich in Klang oder Intensität verändert – zum Beispiel anhaltender oder klagender wirkt
Ob Episoden auch tagsüber auftreten oder häufiger werden
Anzeichen von Unwohlsein: ungewöhnliches Sitzen, Verstecken, verändertes Fell oder Körperhaltung
what_would_change_the_next_step: Das Schreien wird deutlich häufiger, intensiver oder klingt klagend statt spielerisch
Neue Symptome treten auf: Veränderungen beim Fressen oder Trinken, auffälliges Toilettenverhalten, Erbrechen, Verstecken
Die Katze wirkt tagsüber teilnahmslos, weniger beweglich oder allgemein verändert
Die Episoden beginnen auch tagsüber oder weiten sich zeitlich aus
what_you_can_do_now: Beobachte, ob die Episoden immer zur selben Zeit stattfinden und ob sie mit bestimmten Orten in der Wohnung verknüpft sind – das hilft, mögliche äußere Auslöser einzugrenzen.

Falls die Katze abends wenig Beschäftigung hat, kannst du versuchsweise eine kurze interaktive Spieleinheit am frühen Abend einbauen und beobachten, ob sich das nächtliche Muster dadurch verändert – ohne Ergebnis zu erwarten.
Notiere kurz, wann die Episoden stattfinden und wie sie sich anhören, damit du bei Bedarf klare Informationen für den Tierarzt hast.

input.behavior: He's started eating grass obsessively on every walk, then vomiting within an hour. It's happened 4 times this week.
input.whenItHappens: Right after walks, within an hour.

assessment.headline: Repeated grass-eating and vomiting, with reduced appetite and lower energy
assessment.bottom_line: Four vomiting episodes in one week, combined with eating less and more tiredness, goes beyond an isolated stomach upset. Because he is also on Rimadyl, these changes are worth a prompt veterinary conversation.

what_you_reported: Grass-eating on every walk this week, followed by vomiting within an hour, four times in total
This pattern is new — no prior history of this behavior was noted
Eating less at meals over the same period
Currently taking Rimadyl for joint pain

what_could_explain_it.possibility: GI irritation or an underlying stomach issue prompting him to eat grass
what_could_explain_it.why_it_could_fit: Dogs sometimes seek out grass when their stomach is bothering them, and repeated vomiting with reduced appetite and lower energy points toward something affecting his digestive tract.
what_would_make_it_more_or_less_plausibl: More plausible if the vomiting contains bile or appears to happen on an empty stomach
More plausible if he seems uncomfortable or restless before eating the grass
Less plausible if appetite and energy return to normal between episodes

what_could_explain_it.possibility: GI side effect related to Rimadyl use
what_could_explain_it.why_it_could_fit: NSAIDs like Rimadyl can irritate the stomach lining in some dogs, and the combination of vomiting, reduced appetite, and lower energy are changes worth flagging to the vet who manages that medication.
what_would_make_it_more_or_less_plausibl: More plausible if the symptoms started around a change in dosing schedule or if he takes Rimadyl on an empty stomach
More plausible if the vomit contains blood or dark material — contact your vet promptly if you see that
Less plausible if he has been on the same Rimadyl routine for a long time with no previous stomach issues

what_could_explain_it.possibility: Something ingested on walks triggering the vomiting, with grass-eating as a separate behavior
what_could_explain_it.why_it_could_fit: It is also possible he is encountering something on walks — a plant, substance, or material — that is causing the vomiting, and the grass-eating is incidental.
what_would_make_it_more_or_less_plausibl: More plausible if the route has changed recently or includes areas where he sniffs or mouths things beyond grass
More plausible if the vomiting happens even on days he eats less grass
Less plausible if restricting his access to grass during walks reduces the vomiting

what_to_watch: Any blood or dark material in the vomit — that would make veterinary contact more urgent
Whether appetite continues to drop or he stops eating altogether
Whether the tiredness deepens — less willing to move, difficulty getting up
Whether vomiting is increasing in frequency or happening when he has not eaten grass
Any signs of abdominal discomfort such as hunching, reluctance to have his belly touched, or unusual posturing
what_would_change_the_next_step: Blood or dark coffee-ground-like material in the vomit — contact your vet the same day
Complete refusal to eat or drink
Obvious pain, collapse, or significant distress
Vomiting that continues even when grass access is limited on walks
what_you_can_do_now: Contact your vet to describe the full picture — four vomiting episodes, reduced appetite, lower energy, and current Rimadyl use — and let them advise on next steps
On walks, you can try limiting how much grass he eats to see whether that reduces vomiting; note whether it makes a difference
Keep a brief log of each episode: time, how much grass he ate, what the vomit looked like, and whether he had eaten a meal beforehand — this will help your vet assess the pattern
Do not adjust or stop the Rimadyl on your own; that decision belongs with the vet who prescribed it

what_to_record: Time of each vomiting episode and what the vomit looked like
How much he ate at each meal relative to normal
Whether grass access on a walk correlates with vomiting that day
His current Rimadyl dose, schedule, and whether he takes it with food
questions_or_details_to_bring: Could Rimadyl be contributing to the stomach upset, and should any precautions change?
Are the reduced appetite and lower energy connected to the vomiting, or do they need separate evaluation?
What signs should prompt me to bring him in sooner rather than waiting for a scheduled appointment?

input.question: What if she also starts limping?

assessment.headline: Nighttime yowling and bursts of activity

output.answer:
Limping is a separate physical symptom from the nighttime yowling, so it would warrant a vet visit rather than continued watching at home — do not wait to see if it resolves on its own. A cat that is suddenly reluctant to bear weight on a limb could have a joint injury, a paw injury, a muscle problem, or something else entirely; there is no way to tell without an exam.

If the limp appears alongside the yowling and activity bursts, mention both to your vet — the combination gives them more to work with, even if the two things turn out to be unrelated.

One thing to check right away: look at the affected paw and leg for anything visible, like a cut, swelling, or something caught between the toes. If you see swelling, she cannot put any weight on it at all, or she seems to be in significant distress, treat that as urgent and contact a vet or emergency clinic the same day.
